findings.class: E-17 cross-row contradiction + byte-false locational count (WEB/MT numbering-hazard artifact)
findings.defective_text: אך opens (oshb:Ps.62.2) אַ֣ךְ, oshb:Ps.62.3, and (oshb:Ps.62.5) אַ֤ךְ inside this row, plus 2 more later in the psalm
findings.byte_evidence: Verse-initial אך in Psalm 62 sits at MT 62.2, 62.3, 62.5, 62.6, 62.7 and 62.10 - token 1 of each of those six verses is אך at skeleton tier (consonantal_index.json), and sweep.py --skel with the particle spliced from oshb:Ps.62.3 token 1 returns exactly those six Ps 62 verses. This row spans WEB Ps.62.1-Ps.62.6 = MT 62.2-62.7 (its own boundary_evidence_refs close on "web:Ps.62.6 = oshb:Ps.62.7"), so FIVE of the six fall inside the row, not three: oshb:Ps.62.6 = אַ֣ךְ לֵ֭אלֹהִים דּ֣וֹמִּי נַפְשִׁ֑י כִּי מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ תִּקְוָתִֽי (byte tier), quoted in this row's own boundary_rationale as the ring return, and oshb:Ps.62.7 = אַךְ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י לֹ֣א אֶמּֽוֹט (byte tier), which this row's own observed_substrate_signals[1] calls "this row's own closing verse"; only ONE, MT 62.10 = אַ֤ךְ הֶ֥בֶל בְּנֵֽי אָדָם֮ כָּזָ֪ב בְּנֵ֫י אִ֥ישׁ בְּמֹאזְנַ֥יִם לַעֲל֑וֹת הֵ֝֗מָּה מֵהֶ֥בֶל יָֽחַד (byte tier), is later in the psalm. The post-repair neighbour M8-Ps-173 also places the seventh verse inside this row ("Past the psalm's refrain return at oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6)").
findings.proposed_cure: Write that אך opens five verses inside this row (oshb:Ps.62.2, 62.3, 62.5, 62.6, 62.7) with one more later in the psalm (oshb:Ps.62.10), leaving the true total of 6 verse-initial occurrences among Psalm 62's 12 MT body verses unchanged.

findings.class: count-object discipline (contained-substring trap: the digit's object is the substring, not the particle the sentence names)
findings.defective_text: a separate contiguous-consonantal-substring sweep finds 34 verses (36 token-occurrences) book-wide at skeleton tier
findings.byte_evidence: sweep.py --skel with the particle spliced from oshb:Ps.62.3 token 1 (object = the two-consonant skeleton אך; unit = verses) returns count_unit "verses" with skeleton 34, and token_occurrences_skeleton 36 under --tokens, so both digits are byte-true FOR THE SUBSTRING OBJECT. But 12 of those 34 verses carry no standalone particle at all - the hit sits inside a longer word: MT 34.8 מלאך, 35.5 and 35.6 ומלאך, 45.7 / 89.5 / 89.15 / 93.2 כסאך, 77.12 / 88.13 / 89.6 פלאך, 86.7 אקראך, 121.8 ובואך (skeleton tier, token scan of consonantal_index.json over the sweep's own hit set). Word-bound, the particle stands at 22 verses / 24 token-occurrences book-wide. The sentence's subject is the particle, so the 34/36 digits name a different object - the contained-substring trap the hazard catalog names first, the same class it resolves for סלה by giving the word-bound figure.
findings.proposed_cure: Give the word-bound figure for the particle (22 verses / 24 token-occurrences book-wide at skeleton tier), or say in the same clause that the 34/36 substring digits include contained forms.

rows.grounds: Both docket items were re-checked from bytes and both are cured; the row fails on a live byte-false locational count that the repair re-emitted unchanged in the field it edited. Item 1 (medium, observed_substrate_signals[1]): the ordered defect - "carries two further tokens beyond that match (לֹא אֶמּ֥וֹט רַבָּֽה) that oshb:Ps.62.7 lacks" - is gone, and the replacement re-derives exactly. I spliced oshb:Ps.62.3 (8 tokens) and oshb:Ps.62.7 (7 tokens) from verse_map_oshb.json and compared them codepoint by codepoint: tokens 1-5 (אַךְ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י) are identical, and collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.62.3 and --ref oshb:Ps.62.7 with that five-token run spliced out of the packet both return tier byte, so "whose opening five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3 byte-for-byte" is exact and not over-tiered; tokens 6-7 are skeleton-identical (לא אמוט in both, consonantal_index.json) and the only differing codepoints are U+05A3 on oshb:Ps.62.7 token 6, and U+05A5 on oshb:Ps.62.3 token 7 against U+05BD (verse-final silluq) on oshb:Ps.62.7 token 7 - all cantillation marks, no vowel or consonant differing - so "differing only in accents" holds, though the pair is NOT identical at accent_stripped tier (that tier retains U+05BD) and the row rightly names skeleton; and רַבָּֽה collates byte at oshb:Ps.62.3 alone, its verse-final token 8, so "one further token ... which oshb:Ps.62.7 lacks" is byte-true. Item 2 (low, count-object): the ordered unit-naming is installed in BOTH ordered places - observed_substrate_signals[0] now reads "34 verses (36 token-occurrences) book-wide at skeleton tier" and the boundary_rationale parenthetical now reads "34 verses / 36 token-occurrences book-wide at skeleton tier" - and sweep.py --skel with the particle spliced from oshb:Ps.62.3 token 1 returns count_unit "verses" 34 with token_occurrences_skeleton 36, so the digits and the unit re-derive; the retained low finding is that the swept object is the contiguous substring rather than the particle. Every other installed and retained claim re-derives: each Hebrew run in the row collates at byte tier against the ref it names - oshb:Ps.62.2 for the opening ring run, for the אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים pair and for יְשׁוּעָתִֽי; oshb:Ps.62.6 for the return run, for לֵ֭אלֹהִים and for תִּקְוָתִֽי; oshb:Ps.62.3 and oshb:Ps.62.7 both for the shared five-token run; oshb:Ps.62.3 for רַבָּֽה; oshb:Ps.62.5 for the pointed particle cited there - and collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.62.6 with the FULL spliced oshb:Ps.62.2 returns tier none, so "shares no tier" holds and the lexical-substitution argument stands. The title claim holds: verse_map_oshb.json maps oshb:Ps.62.1 to web:Ps.62.0 under the shift+1 rule, the title is one counted MT verse, and the opening row carries "web:Ps.62.0 = oshb:Ps.62.1" in boundary_evidence_refs as the ruled strategy requires. "One of 3 Ps psalms so labeled, with Psalms 39 and 77" re-derives - the skeleton sweep of the Jeduthun label returns Ps.39.1, Ps.62.1 and Ps.77.1, matching the strategy's byte-verified membership {39, 62, 77}. "12 MT body verses" re-derives (MT Psalm 62 runs 13 verses, v1 the counted title). Selah is disclosed correctly and non-drivingly: the psalm's two Selah verses are MT 62.5, inside this span and disclosed here as closing web:Ps.62.4, and MT 62.9, outside it and disclosed by M8-Ps-173, so span-scoped symmetry is satisfied and the row says outright it is not the driver. Both sides of both seams were weighed under the book seam law. Front seam: preceding close oshb:Ps.61.9 = כֵּ֤ן אֲזַמְּרָ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֣ לָעַ֑ד לְֽשַׁלְּמִ֥י נְדָרַ֗י י֣וֹם יֽוֹם (byte tier; M8-Ps-171's last verse, web:Ps.61.8) against following onset oshb:Ps.62.1 = לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל יְדוּת֗וּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד (byte tier; the superscription, tier-1 opener evidence) and body onset oshb:Ps.62.2 = אַ֣ךְ אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּעָתִֽי (byte tier) - a psalm boundary, and the two rows argue it coherently, M8-Ps-171 closing Psalm 61 on its vow bracket. Rear seam: close oshb:Ps.62.7 = אַךְ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י לֹ֣א אֶמּֽוֹט (byte tier; the refrain return, whose first five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3) against onset oshb:Ps.62.8 = עַל אֱ֭לֹהִים יִשְׁעִ֣י וּכְבוֹדִ֑י צוּר עֻזִּ֥י מַ֝חְסִ֗י בֵּֽאלֹהִֽים (byte tier), which M8-Ps-173 argues from צוּר עֻזִּ֥י echoing the refrain's own צ֭וּרִי plus the plural-imperative register shift one verse in - each row claims the seam once, with no overlap and no gap. Tiling survives: WEB Ps.62.1-62.6 here plus M8-Ps-173's Ps.62.7-62.12 covers Psalm 62's 12 WEB body verses exactly, and the previous row ends Psalm 61 at web:Ps.61.8. Dependent fields stay coherent with the unchanged span: unit_type strophe under the ruled vocabulary for a six-verse strophe inside a twelve-verse psalm, parent_psalm 62, confidence high carried by byte-tier ring evidence, and a strongest_rejected_alternative that still names the rival the envelope argument defeats. E-17 pass: no unexpanded placeholder tokens; no erratum, reviewer, tool or id talk in any prose field (the only "M8-Ps" and "attempt" strings in the row are the schema fields decision_id and writer_attempt_id); no tier-4 metadata doing driver or corroboration work, since no WEB punctuation, paragraphing or heading is cited anywhere; no gloss overshoot, with all three curly-quoted WEB runs verifying verbatim; and the repair introduced no new universal. The order recorded no legitimate alternative, so nothing is owed under disclosed uncertainty. Neighbour coherence is otherwise improved rather than harmed - the repaired observed_substrate_signals[1] now matches M8-Ps-173's own "whose opening five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3 byte-for-byte" wording, curing the seam-pair mismatch that was routed from that row - but observed_substrate_signals[0] contradicts both it and this row's own boundary_rationale. The pipeline-owned fields were read only from repaired_row_as_shipped (chunk_index_in_book 172; no final_sha256 carried on the slice row) and are part of no finding.
